title: Synthesis of Cu2O@Cu-Fe-K Prussian Blue analogue core–shell nanocube for enhanced electroreduction of CO2 to multi-carbon products
abstract: Cu2O@Cu-Fe-K Prussian Blue analogue (K-PBA) core–shell nanocube was synthesized by a facile template-engaged redox deposition approach, and could be used as an efficient catalyst for CO2 electrochemical reduction (CO2ER). The presence of K-PBA shell not only can protect the Cu2O active core, but also promote the ratios of multi-carbon products to competing methane in CO2ER, achieving a total C2+ Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 23.9% (ethylene 10.8%, ethanol 3.6% and n-propanol 9.5%) at 1.11 V (vs. reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), while jtotal = 6.2 mA cm . It is suggested that K-PBA shell coating alter inherent adsorption energetics of Cu2O, which contributes to the C–C coupling step in CO2ER. 2019 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved.

sections.heading: 1. Introduction
sections.text:
Reducing atmospheric CO2 into high energy densities multicarbon products to solve the energy crisis and environmental issues is highly attractive. Although Cu based materials were mostly investigated as a class of high active catalysts in CO2ER, the complex multi-step pathways for C2+ products formation make them occur at very negative potentials and lack selectivity. Previous research has shown that the origin of Cu based materials’ poor selectivity for C2+ products is mainly due to its moderate binding energy could absorb mostly reactive intermediates [1,2]. Therefore, via the surface and interface engineering modulation to change the binding energy for different intermediates is a possible way to optimize the Cu based materials’ selectivity. To date, introducing another metal species to form alloy or bimetallic materials seems to be an efficient way to achieve a high selectivity. For example, the experimental results of Cu-Au system has been proved that increased Au content in Cu-Au alloy can enhance the CO production, and suppress the methane pathway [3,4]. In addition, a range
of elements such as Ag, Zn, Pd, Sn and Bi has also reported can influence the Cu interface engineering [5–9].
Cu2O, which has been wildly used as the precursor to prepare the Cu-based material, was already proved to be able to increase the selectivity towards multi-carbon products in CO2ER, due to its high contents of Cu(I) species [2,10–12]. Therefore, exploring the binding energy of Cu2O surface changes and increasing the stability of Cu(I) species may help to achieve a higher selectivity for C2+ production [13].
Herein, a Cu2O@Fe-Cu-K PBA (Cu2O@K-PBA) core-shell CO2ER catalyst was synthesized via a template-engaged redox deposition approach, where Cu2O was used as self-template precipitating with potassium ferricyanide (K3[Fe(CN)6]) to introduce Fe element. Electrochemical measurement results indicate that K-PBA shell coating can efficiently enhance the C2+ products formation and suppress the CH4 step, showing more than twice higher C2H4/CH4 ratio than original Cu2O.
2. Experimental
All chemicals were of analytical grade and used without further purification. The details of synthesis process, characterizations and CO2ER tests were given in the Supplementary information (SI).

sections.heading: 3. Results and discussion
sections.text:

XRD patterns were used to prove the phases’ changes in each step. As shown in Fig. 1b, after K3[Fe(CN)6] oxidation, several weak peaks occurred at 16.9 , 18.0 , 24.8 , 25.6 and 34.2 except obviously Cu2O peaks, which assigned to (0 0 2), (2 0 0), (2 0 2), (2 2 0) and (0 0 4) planes of K2Cu[Fe(CN)6]. No Cu2O signals can be found after aqueous HCl etching, indicating that Cu2O was completely removed. In addition, the phase of K-PBA also changed after aqueous HCl etching, making the composition changes to Cu2[Fe (CN)6] [14]. The SEM (Fig. S1) and TEM (Fig. 1 c-h) images clearly revealed the structure transformation. It can be seen that after being oxidized by K3[Fe(CN)6], the cubic Cu2O templates with sizes of 300 nm are uniformly covered with 10–20 nm flaky shells. Moreover, these well inherited flaky shells with cubic voids inside can be clearly observed after removing Cu2O cores.
XPS was used to analysis the various valence states of different metal ions in Cu2O@K-PBA composite. As shown in Fig. 2a, Cu, Fe,
K, N, O and C elements were found in XPS survey, conforming to the composition of Cu2O@K-PBA (K2Cu[Fe(CN)6]). Besides, both Cu1+/0 (2p3/2 932.7 eV and 2p1/2 953.2 eV) and Cu2+ (2p3/2 934.9 eV and 2p1/2 954.5 eV) peaks can be fitted in Cu 2p spectrum, corresponding to Cu1+ in Cu2O core and Cu2+ in K-PBA shell [15]. Two peaks located at 708 eV and 720.9 eV can be assigned to Fe2+ 2p1/2 and Fe2+ 2p3/2 [14], indicating that excessive [Fe(III) (CN)6]3- cannot coprecipitate with Cu2+.
The CO2ER performances of different catalysts obtained from each steps were given in Fig. 3. The relative tests show that Cu2O@K-PBA has a larger current density and smaller charge transfer resistance than Cu2O (Fig. S2), suggesting its higher electrocatalytic activity. The durability shown in Fig. S3 suggests that Cu2O and Cu2O@K-PBA can be used as a possible CO2ER catalyst. As shown in Fig. 3a-c, both FEs of C2H4 increase with the increase in overpotentials, while the FEs of CH4 synchronically dropped in the same voltage range. However, even with the similar trend, the Cu2O@K-PBA also shows a higher ethylene/methane ratio (11.4) than Cu2O (5.6), particularly at negative potentials. This may be because that the dimerization and protonation steps are started with the same *CO intermediates, leading to the competition between C2H4 and CH4 formation (Fig. 3d) [16]. With the K-PBA coating, a dipole field was created out of the Cu2O, which can stabilize the adsorption of intermediates with significant dipole moments (eg. *CO2, *CO and *OCCO) promoting the C–C coupling step [17–18].

Not only for gas products, the liquid multi-carbon products also increased, reaching the maximum C2+ Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 23.9% (rethylene = 5.58 lmol m 2 s 1 (FE = 10.8%), rethanol = 1.86 - lmol m 2 s 1 (FE = 3.6%) and rn-propanol = 3.27 lmol m 2 s 1 (FE = 9.5%), no n-propanol can be found in Cu2O sample (Fig. S4))
at 1.11 V vs. RHE (jtotal = 6.2 mA cm 2), which is higher than other Cu2O based catalysts (Table S1) [12]. Interestingly, a strongly HER was displayed (FE more than 80%) in aqueous HCl etching sample (Fig. S5), indicating that the alkali-metal K in PBA frame plays an essential role in suppressing Fe HER activity [1,17,18].

sections.heading: 4. Conclusions
sections.text: In summary, we employed K-PBA shell to introduce different elements achieving an interface engineering modulation towards Cu2O surface. The results show that the synergistic effects between Cu2O core and K-PBA shell can efficient boost the selectivity of C2+ products formation in CO2ER. Moreover, the K element in PBA frame can efficiently suppress the Fe HER activity. This study presents template-engaged redox deposition as a new way to exploit bimetal effects and core/shell structure for high selectivity CO2ER catalysts designing.
